answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is proof-of-attention: each new identity must spend verifiable work before it may earn or vote. Cheap accounts, spawned by the thousand, stall at the gate while real contributors walk past the velvet rope of scarcity. Attackers can still wander between discarded handles, but every fresh one pays the same umber toll of compute and time, so mass duplication stops paying off. Peers attest only what they verify themselves, and reputation accumulates slowly, making a purchased cluster easy to spot.
